messages:
mira: Quick RFC follow-up — propose a lightweight operator API that binds tenant SLAs to capacity contracts and emits backpressure signals to the serving layer. Want to align on interface boundaries before I open a formal PR.
aj: Can you sketch the division of responsibilities? is this a new autoscaler or a policy layer? :thinking_face:
mira: Not another monolithic autoscaler. Idea is 2-layer: 1) Policy/contract engine where tenants declare SLOs (latency P95, qps, cost ceiling) and contract constraints, 2) an allocator/operator that reconciles infra (GPU pools, reservations) and exposes a small signal API to the runtime.
cheng: So runtime still handles admission & prewarm, and operator only provisions capacity and publishes signals? how do we encode temporary burst rights?
mira: Exactly. Runtime stays responsible for low-latency admission, prewarm, and per-request routing. Operator publishes two things: a) PoolContract objects (declared desired headroom + min guarantees + burst credits) and b) Signal streams: reserve_granted/declined, predicted_headroom(t+N), and backpressure_hint.
aj: Does PoolContract need a full CRD? could be just annotations on tenant resource to avoid duplication.
mira: Thinking CRD helps for visibility & reconciliation. Proposal snippet:
```yaml
apiVersion: infra.redwood/v1alpha
kind: PoolContract
metadata:
  name: tenant-foo-contract
spec:
  tenant: tenant-foo
  guarantee:
    gpus: 2
    min_p95_ms: 120
  burst:
    credits: 300
    window_secs: 3600
  costCapUsdPerHour: 5
status:
  allocated:
    pools: ["dedicated-eu-03"]
  nextPredictionTs: 2026-07-01T12:00:00Z
``` 
aj: That helps. How do we prevent oscillation when operator scales up/down? we need hysteresis + predicted demand.
taylor: Add an explicit reconciliation horizon: operator proposes changes with a confidence score and runtime accepts/rejects with a forced-commit API. If runtime rejects (e.g., prewarm insufficient), operator keeps trying with different pools.
devon: What about private deployments? operator can't provision cloud GPUs there.
mira: For Private, PoolContract maps to a logical capacity token. Operator still emits predicted_headroom/backpressure but provisioning step is a no-op; platform teams can manually reconcile or run a local operator variant.
cheng: Admission control needs an extensible hook to interpret backpressure_hint. propose small API:
```json
{ "tenant": "tenant-foo", "timestamp": 1620000000, "hint": "soft_throttle", "severity": "medium" }
```
runtime acts accordingly (degraded batching, lower tokens, route to cheaper model)
aj: Nice. Who owns the costCap enforcement? operator or billing pipeline?
mira: Operator enforces soft caps: it refuses new guaranteed capacity if costCap exceeded and emits a CostLimitReached event. Billing pipeline enforces hard accounting and alerts.
infra-bot: deploy pipeline: applied 1 staged change to infra/operator-proto repo (CI passed)
aj: Any long-term refactor considerations? I worry about coupling policy language to our current allocator implementation.
mira: We should define a minimal declarative contract language (guarantees, burst, SLO targets, cost bounds, affinity hints). Keep semantics stable and let allocators implement optimizations underneath. Plan: v1 contract -> one allocator -> gather telemetry -> evolve contract primitives not implementation.
taylor: Experimental plan: implement operator in feature branch, run with 3 tenants on a dedicated staging pool for 2 weeks, capture predicted_headroom vs observed, tune hysteresis.
devon: LGTM. can we add a dashboard metric for "contract_violation_count" and "fraction_of_requests_routed_to_fallback"?
mira: Yes — will add to Console telemetry and create eval prompt set to catch regressions.
aj: sgtm. please open the repo PR and RFC follow-up with the CRD + example mapping. I'll volunteer to review the operator API.
mira: Thanks! I'll spin up the branch and post the PR link when ready. :slightly_smiling_face:
